raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Add native support for [LiquidAI/LFM3-1.7B](https://huggingface.co/LiquidAI/LFM3-1.7B) (`Lfm3ForCausalLM`), step 2 of #64645.

Depends on #64647 by @abhijithneilabraham (width-7 `causal_conv1d`). That commit is included here unchanged, with its original authorship, so this branch runs and CI can exercise the model. It can be dropped on rebase once #64647 merges.

## Claims

- New `vllm/model_executor/models/lfm3.py`: the 24-layer hybrid (13 short-conv, 6 full-attention, 5 sliding-window attention with window 256), QK RMSNorm, a per-head sigmoid attention output gate, sandwich norms and tied embeddings.
- Reuses `ShortConv` (width 7), `Lfm2MLP`, the LFM2 weight mapper and the existing `proportional` RoPE. No changes to core components.
- Registered in the model registry and test registry, added to `HYBRID_MODELS` in `test_hybrid.py`, and documented in `supported_models.md`.
- Serving works with the existing parsers: `--reasoning-parser qwen3 --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder --enable-auto-tool-choice`.

## Validation

**Environment:** A100-SXM4-40GB, torch 2.14.0+cu130, transformers 5.22.1, triton 3.8.0, BF16. Branch base: `fac2ce2eb`. Checkpoint revision: `ac2586a34f1a1c03329dbdcdefabd8b6478ddaa7`.

| Check | Command | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Kernels (with #64647) | `pytest tests/kernels/mamba/test_causal_conv1d.py` | 324 passed |
| Registry / init | `pytest "tests/models/test_registry.py::test_registry_imports[Lfm3ForCausalLM]" tests/models/test_registry.py::test_hf_registry_coverage "tests/models/test_initialization.py::test_can_initialize_large_subset[Lfm3ForCausalLM]"` | 3 passed |
| HF comparison | `pytest tests/models/language/generation/test_hybrid.py -k LFM3` | passed (`check_logprobs_close` against the HF remote-code reference) |
| Serving | `vllm serve LiquidAI/LFM3-1.7B --trust-remote-code --reasoning-parser qwen3 --tool-call-parser qwen3_coder --enable-auto-tool-choice` | completions, chat, 16 concurrent requests, reasoning on/off, tool call + tool-result round trip, streaming tool call: all passed |
| GSM8K | `tests/evals/gsm8k` evaluator, 5-shot, `/v1/completions`, greedy, full test set (1319) | **0.4587 ± 0.0137** |

<details>
<summary>Greedy parity vs HF (64 tokens, 8 prompts)</summary>

An additional greedy comparison against the HF reference used 8 prompts, including 331- and 609-token prompts that cross the 256-token window.

- **Single-request mode:** 5/8 prompts match exactly. In batched mode it is 3/8.
- **Where they diverge:** each divergence comes after 31–53 matching tokens, at near-ties. The top-1 vs top-2 logprob gap is ≤ 0.125 (three are exact ties), and the top-5 sets fully overlap.
- **Before divergence:** chosen-token logprobs differ by ≤ 0.12.
- **vLLM against itself:** single-request vs batched vLLM output shows the same kind of divergence (6/8 exact), so these are bf16 numerics rather than a modeling difference.
- **609-token prompt:** matches HF exactly.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Benchmarks (A100-40GB, BF16, max-model-len 4096)</summary>

| Benchmark | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `vllm bench latency --input-len 512 --output-len 128 --batch-size 1` | 0.566 s avg (p99 0.568 s) |
| `vllm bench latency --input-len 512 --output-len 128 --batch-size 8` | 0.628 s avg (p99 0.633 s) |
| `vllm bench throughput --dataset-name random --num-prompts 200 --input-len 1024 --output-len 256` | 26.2 req/s, 33.6k tok/s |

</details>

## Details

- **RoPE:** the checkpoint config says `rope_type: default` for full attention with `partial_rotary_factor: 0.5`. The reference implementation keeps the full-head frequency progression for the rotated dimensions and zero-pads the tail, using NeoX pairing over all 128 dims. This is not vLLM's standard partial rotary (`rotary_dim=64`), so full-attention layers select the existing `proportional` RoPE (`Gemma4RotaryEmbedding`), which implements exactly this layout. Sliding layers use full rotary with theta 1e4.
- **Config:** transformers does not ship `Lfm3Config` yet (huggingface/transformers#50036 is open), so `trust_remote_code=True` is needed for the config. Execution uses the native model.
- **Duplicates:** no other LFM3 model PR is open. #64647 is only the kernel dependency.
- **Not validated yet:** TP/PP, quantization, LoRA, speculative decoding and prefix-caching reuse.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

@atmikshetty I believe the merge of this PR requires the transformers PR from @paulpak58 from liquidAI to be merged (https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/50036 (model), https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/50035)

Thanks! Right, `Lfm3Config` isn't in a transformers release yet (huggingface/transformers#50036). Until then this PR loads the config via `trust_remote_code` from the checkpoint, and execution uses the native vLLM model, so it works with current transformers (validation in the description was run that way). Happy to follow whatever maintainers prefer: wait for #50036, or vendor `Lfm3Config` under `vllm/transformers_utils/configs/` in the meantime.

The description lists quantization and LoRA as not validated yet. I had an LFM3 port of my own that is nearly identical to this PR, so I ran those checks on it, plus IFEval, on a different GPU. The results are below in case they help review.

**Scope.** These numbers come from my own branch, not from this PR's head. The model code differs from `lfm3.py` here in only a few places:
- I don't set `ignore_unexpected_prefixes` for a tied `lm_head`.
- I don't pass `num_spec` to `short_conv_state_shape`, the same as `lfm2.py`.
- I map to `proportional` RoPE only when `partial_rotary_factor < 1`, and raise for a partial factor with a non-default `rope_type`.

None of these touches the quantized or LoRA code paths. The kernel is #64647's change plus a width guard (suggested there).

**Environment:** RTX 4070 Ti SUPER (sm_89, 16 GB), torch 2.14.0+cu130, transformers 5.22.1, Triton 3.8.0, base `3d23773f10`. Server: `vllm serve ... --trust-remote-code --max-model-len 32768 --reasoning-parser deepseek_r1`.

**Tests on this GPU:** `test_causal_conv1d.py` 324 passed, the registry/init tests 3 passed, and `test_hybrid.py -k LFM3` passed.

### GSM8K 5-shot and the generation config

| `--generation-config` | `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, 5-shot, greedy, 256 tokens, 1319 questions |
|---|---|
| default (`auto`) | 46.2% |
| `vllm` | 41.7% |

The default 46.2% agrees with the 45.87% in the description. The checkpoint's `generation_config.json` sets `repetition_penalty: 1.1`, and with the default `--generation-config auto` the server merges it into every request, which makes up the difference. I ran the other evals with `--generation-config vllm`, so the card's sampling settings below are the only ones applied.

I also sent the first 200 questions through Transformers greedy, with the repetition penalty removed. Transformers and vLLM both scored 39.0%, and 166 of the 200 extracted answers were the same.

### Accuracy, BF16 and Liquid's quantized checkpoints

The card's settings are thinking on. GSM8K uses temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95 and top_k 20. IFEval uses lm-eval 0.4.13 `local-chat-completions` at temperature 0.6, top_p 0.95 and `max_gen_toks` 16384.

| Checkpoint | Kernel on sm_89 | GSM8K, 0-shot chat, 1319 questions | IFEval prompt strict / prompt loose / inst strict / inst loose |
|---|---|---|---|
| LFM3-1.7B (BF16) | — | 87.2 | 95.38 / 96.67 / 96.16 / 97.24 |
| LFM3-1.7B-FP8 (compressed-tensors, 128×128 blocks) | `MarlinFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel` | 86.1 | 93.90 / 96.30 / 95.08 / 96.76 |
| LFM3-1.7B-NVFP4 (ModelOpt) | `MarlinNvFp4LinearKernel` | 86.3 | 94.45 / 94.82 / 95.08 / 95.44 |

The model card gives 96.66 for IFEval.

**Loading.** Both quantized checkpoints load with no LFM3-specific code:
- Their ignore and exclude lists name the conv layers `conv.*`. Those names still match `short_conv` after the weight mapper is applied.
- The conv projections, `gate_proj` and `lm_head` stay BF16, as the model cards state.
- NVFP4 also leaves attention unquantized.

sm_89 runs both checkpoints through the weight-only Marlin kernels, so the native W8A8 block-FP8 and W4A4 NVFP4 paths on Hopper and Blackwell are not covered here.

### LoRA

The adapters are rank 8 and use the checkpoint's own module names:
- **Attention:** `q/k/v/o_proj` and `gate_proj`.
- **Conv:** `conv.in_proj` and `conv.out_proj`.
- **MLP:** `w1/w2/w3`.

Each run used 32 greedy tokens.

| Check | BF16 | FP8 | NVFP4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Zero-B adapter gives output identical to the base model | yes | yes | yes |
| Random adapter changes the output | yes | yes | yes |
| Adapter nonzero only on `conv.in_proj`/`conv.out_proj` changes the output | yes | yes | yes |
| Adapter nonzero only on `gate_proj` changes the output | yes | yes | no token flipped (see below) |

The conv-only and gate-only adapters target the two places where an adapter could be silently dropped: the `.conv.` → `.short_conv.` rename and the single-slice `in_proj` packing.

**NVFP4 gate-only.** The gate-only adapter flipped no token on NVFP4, but it is applied. Its `gate_proj` is a `ColumnParallelLinearWithLoRA`, and it shifts the logprobs by about as much as on BF16 (mean 0.02, max 0.11).

**Mixed batches.** I mixed base, zero-adapter and random-adapter requests in one batch. Compared with separate runs, the only differences were divergences at near-ties, where each token was in the other's top 5. That is expected without batch invariance.

Once this PR merges, I can follow up with a CI test for the quantized checkpoints and LoRA, if that would be useful.

**Scope.** These numbers come from my own branch ([hungho77/vllm@feat/lfm3](https://github.com/hungho77/vllm/tree/feat/lfm3)), not from this PR's head.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to write this comment and the evaluation scripts. I ran the measurements myself.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Inference-only LFM3 model.
+
+LFM3 extends LFM2 with sliding-window attention layers, a per-head sigmoid
+output gate, sandwich norms and zero-tail ("proportional") partial RoPE on
+full-attention layers.
+"""
+
+from collections.abc import Iterable
+from itertools import islice
+
+import torch
+import torch.nn as nn
+from transformers import PreTrainedConfig
+
+from vllm.compilation.decorators import support_torch_compile
+from vllm.config import CacheConfig, ModelConfig, VllmConfig
+from vllm.distributed import get_pp_group, get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.attention import Attention
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.layernorm import RMSNorm
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.linear import (
+    ColumnParallelLinear,
+    QKVParallelLinear,
+    RowParallelLinear,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.logits_processor import LogitsProcessor
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.mamba.mamba_utils import (
+    MambaStateCopyFunc,
+    MambaStateCopyFuncCalculator,
+    MambaStateDtypeCalculator,
+    MambaStateShapeCalculator,
+)
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.mamba.short_conv import ShortConv
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.quantization import QuantizationConfig
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.rotary_embedding import get_rope
+from vllm.model_executor.layers.vocab_parallel_embedding import (
+    ParallelLMHead,
+    VocabParallelEmbedding,
+)
+from vllm.sequence import IntermediateTensors
+
+from .interfaces import HasInnerState, IsHybrid, SupportsLoRA, SupportsPP, SupportsQuant
+from .lfm2 import Lfm2MLP, Lfm2Model
+from .utils import (
+    AutoWeightsLoader,
+    PPMissingLayer,
+    extract_layer_index,
+    make_empty_intermediate_tensors_factory,
+    make_layers,
+    maybe_prefix,
+)
+
+
+class Lfm3Attention(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        config: PreTrainedConfig,
+        layer_idx: int,
+        cache_config: CacheConfig | None = None,
+        quant_config: QuantizationConfig | None = None,
+        prefix: str = "",
+    ) -> None:
+        super().__init__()
+        self.hidden_size = config.hidden_size
+        tp_size = get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size()
+        self.total_num_heads = config.num_attention_heads
+        assert self.total_num_heads % tp_size == 0
+        self.num_heads = self.total_num_heads // tp_size
+        self.total_num_kv_heads = config.num_key_value_heads
+        if self.total_num_kv_heads >= tp_size:
+            assert self.total_num_kv_heads % tp_size == 0
+        else:
+            assert tp_size % self.total_num_kv_heads == 0
+        self.num_kv_heads = max(1, self.total_num_kv_heads // tp_size)
+        self.head_dim = config.head_dim
+        self.q_size = self.num_heads * self.head_dim
+        self.kv_size = self.num_kv_heads * self.head_dim
+        self.scaling = self.head_dim**-0.5
+
+        self.qkv_proj = QKVParallelLinear(
+            hidden_size=self.hidden_size,
+            head_size=self.head_dim,
+            total_num_heads=self.total_num_heads,
+            total_num_kv_heads=self.total_num_kv_heads,
+            bias=False,
+            quant_config=quant_config,
+            prefix=f"{prefix}.qkv_proj",
+        )
+        self.gate_proj = ColumnParallelLinear(
+            self.hidden_size,
+            self.total_num_heads,
+            bias=False,
+            quant_config=quant_config,
+            prefix=f"{prefix}.gate_proj",
+        )
+        self.o_proj = RowParallelLinear(
+            input_size=self.total_num_heads * self.head_dim,
+            output_size=self.hidden_size,
+            bias=False,
+            quant_config=quant_config,
+            prefix=f"{prefix}.o_proj",
+        )
+
+        layer_type = config.layer_types[layer_idx]
+        rope_parameters = dict(config.rope_parameters[layer_type])
+        # LFM3 keeps the full-head-dim frequency progression for the rotated
+        # dims and leaves the tail unrotated, which is what "proportional"
+        # RoPE implements.
+        if rope_parameters.get("rope_type", "default") == "default":
+            rope_parameters["rope_type"] = "proportional"
+        self.rotary_emb = get_rope(
+            self.head_dim,
+            max_position=config.max_position_embeddings,
+            rope_parameters=rope_parameters,
+            is_neox_style=True,
+        )
+        sliding_window = (
+            config.sliding_window if layer_type == "sliding_attention" else None
+        )
+        self.attn = Attention(
+            self.num_heads,
+            self.head_dim,
+            self.scaling,
+            num_kv_heads=self.num_kv_heads,
+            cache_config=cache_config,
+            quant_config=quant_config,
+            per_layer_sliding_window=sliding_window,
+            prefix=f"{prefix}.attn",
+        )
+        self.q_norm = RMSNorm(self.head_dim, eps=config.norm_eps)
+        self.k_norm = RMSNorm(self.head_dim, eps=config.norm_eps)
+
+    def forward(
+        self,
+        positions: torch.Tensor,
+        hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        n_tokens, _ = hidden_states.shape
+        qkv, _ = self.qkv_proj(hidden_states)
+        q, k, v = qkv.split([self.q_size, self.kv_size, self.kv_size], dim=-1)
+        q = self.q_norm(q.view(n_tokens, self.num_heads, self.head_dim))
+        k = self.k_norm(k.view(n_tokens, self.num_kv_heads, self.head_dim))
+        q, k = self.rotary_emb(positions, q, k)
+        attn_output = self.attn(
+            q.view(n_tokens, self.q_size), k.view(n_tokens, self.kv_size), v
+        )
+        gate, _ = self.gate_proj(hidden_states)
+        attn_output = attn_output.view(n_tokens, self.num_heads, self.head_dim)
+        attn_output = attn_output * torch.sigmoid(gate).unsqueeze(-1)
+        output, _ = self.o_proj(attn_output.view(n_tokens, self.q_size))
+        return output
+
+
+class Lfm3DecoderLayer(nn.Module):
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        config: PreTrainedConfig,
+        layer_idx: int,
+        model_config: ModelConfig | None = None,
+        cache_config: CacheConfig | None = None,
+        quant_config: QuantizationConfig | None = None,
+        prefix: str = "",
+    ) -> None:
+        super().__init__()
+        self.is_attention_layer = config.layer_types[layer_idx] != "conv"
+        if self.is_attention_layer:
+            self.self_attn = Lfm3Attention(
+                config,
+                layer_idx,
+                cache_config=cache_config,
+                quant_config=quant_config,
+                prefix=f"{prefix}.self_attn",
+            )
+        else:
+            self.short_conv = ShortConv(
+                config=config,
+                dim=config.hidden_size,
+                layer_idx=layer_idx,
+                model_config=model_config,
+                cache_config=cache_config,
+                quant_config=quant_config,
+                prefix=f"{prefix}.short_conv",
+            )
+        self.feed_forward = Lfm2MLP(
+            dim=config.hidden_size,
+            intermediate_size=config.intermediate_size,
+            multiple_of=1,
+            auto_adjust_ff_dim=False,
+            ffn_dim_multiplier=None,
+            quant_config=quant_config,
+            prefix=f"{prefix}.feed_forward",
+        )
+        self.operator_norm = RMSNorm(config.hidden_size, eps=config.norm_eps)
+        self.ffn_norm = RMSNorm(config.hidden_size, eps=config.norm_eps)
+        self.use_sandwich_norm = config.use_sandwich_norm
+        if self.use_sandwich_norm:
+            self.post_operator_norm = RMSNorm(config.hidden_size, eps=config.norm_eps)
+            self.post_ffn_norm = RMSNorm(config.hidden_size, eps=config.norm_eps)
+
+    def forward(
+        self,
+        positions: torch.Tensor,
+        hidden_states: torch.Tensor,
+        residual: torch.Tensor | None,
+    ) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
+        if residual is None:
+            residual = hidden_states
+            hidden_states = self.operator_norm(hidden_states)
+        else:
+            hidden_states, residual = self.operator_norm(hidden_states, residual)
+        if self.is_attention_layer:
+            hidden_states = self.self_attn(positions, hidden_states)
+        else:
+            output = torch.empty_like(hidden_states)
+            self.short_conv(hidden_states, output)
+            hidden_states = output
+        if self.use_sandwich_norm:
+            hidden_states = self.post_operator_norm(hidden_states)
+        hidden_states, residual = self.ffn_norm(hidden_states, residual)
+        hidden_states = self.feed_forward(hidden_states)
+        if self.use_sandwich_norm:
+            hidden_states = self.post_ffn_norm(hidden_states)
+        return hidden_states, residual
+
+
+@support_torch_compile
+class Lfm3Model(nn.Module):
+    hf_to_vllm_mapper = Lfm2Model.hf_to_vllm_mapper
+
+    def __init__(self, *, vllm_config: VllmConfig, prefix: str = ""):
+        super().__init__()
+        config = vllm_config.model_config.hf_config
+        model_config = vllm_config.model_config
+        cache_config = vllm_config.cache_config
+        quant_config = vllm_config.quant_config
+
+        self.config = config
+        self.vocab_size = config.vocab_size
+        self.embed_tokens = VocabParallelEmbedding(self.vocab_size, config.hidden_size)
+
+        def get_layer(prefix: str):
+            return Lfm3DecoderLayer(
+                config,
+                extract_layer_index(prefix),
+                model_config,
+                cache_config,
+                quant_config=quant_config,
+                prefix=prefix,
+            )
+
+        self.start_layer, self.end_layer, self.layers = make_layers(
+            config.num_hidden_layers, get_layer, prefix=f"{prefix}.layers"
+        )
+        self.make_empty_intermediate_tensors = make_empty_intermediate_tensors_factory(
+            ["hidden_states", "residual"], config.hidden_size
+        )
+
+        if get_pp_group().is_last_rank:
+            self.embedding_norm = RMSNorm(config.hidden_size, eps=config.norm_eps)
+        else:
+            self.embedding_norm = PPMissingLayer()
+
+    def embed_input_ids(self, input_ids: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return self.embed_tokens(input_ids)
+
+    def forward(
+        self,
+        input_ids: torch.Tensor | None,
+        positions: torch.Tensor,
+        intermediate_tensors: IntermediateTensors | None = None,
+        inputs_embeds: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor | IntermediateTensors:
+        if get_pp_group().is_first_rank:
+            if inputs_embeds is not None:
+                hidden_states = inputs_embeds
+            else:
+                hidden_states = self.embed_input_ids(input_ids)
+            residual = None
+        else:
+            assert intermediate_tensors is not None
+            hidden_states = intermediate_tensors["hidden_states"]
+            residual = intermediate_tensors["residual"]
+
+        for layer in islice(self.layers, self.start_layer, self.end_layer):
+            hidden_states, residual = layer(positions, hidden_states, residual)
+        if not get_pp_group().is_last_rank:
+            return IntermediateTensors(
+                {"hidden_states": hidden_states, "residual": residual}
+            )
+        hidden_states, _ = self.embedding_norm(hidden_states, residual)
+        return hidden_states
+
+    def load_weights(self, weights: Iterable[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]) -> set[str]:
+        loader = AutoWeightsLoader(self)
+        return loader.load_weights(weights, mapper=self.hf_to_vllm_mapper)
+
+
+class Lfm3ForCausalLM(
+    nn.Module, HasInnerState, SupportsLoRA, SupportsPP, IsHybrid, SupportsQuant
+):
+    packed_modules_mapping = {
+        "qkv_proj": ["q_proj", "k_proj", "v_proj"],
+        "w13": ["w1", "w3"],
+        "in_proj": ["in_proj"],
+    }
+
+    hf_to_vllm_mapper = Lfm3Model.hf_to_vllm_mapper
+
+    embedding_modules = {
+        "embed_tokens": "input_embeddings",
+        "lm_head": "output_embeddings",
+    }
+
+    @classmethod
+    def get_mamba_state_dtype_from_config(
+        cls,
+        vllm_config: "VllmConfig",
+    ) -> tuple[torch.dtype, ...]:
+        return MambaStateDtypeCalculator.short_conv_state_dtype(
+            vllm_config.model_config.dtype,
+            vllm_config.cache_config.mamba_cache_dtype,
+        )
+
+    @classmethod
+    def get_mamba_state_shape_from_config(
+        cls,
+        vllm_config: "VllmConfig",
+    ) -> tuple[tuple[int, int]]:
+        hf_config = vllm_config.model_config.hf_config
+        return MambaStateShapeCalculator.short_conv_state_shape(
+            tp_world_size=vllm_config.parallel_config.tensor_parallel_size,
+            intermediate_size=hf_config.hidden_size,
+            conv_kernel=hf_config.conv_L_cache,
+            num_spec=vllm_config.num_speculative_tokens,
+        )
+
+    @classmethod
+    def get_mamba_state_copy_func(cls) -> tuple[MambaStateCopyFunc]:
+        return MambaStateCopyFuncCalculator.short_conv_state_copy_func()
+
+    def __init__(self, *, vllm_config: VllmConfig, prefix: str = "") -> None:
+        super().__init__()
+        config = vllm_config.model_config.hf_config
+        quant_config = vllm_config.quant_config
+        self.config = config
+        self.model = Lfm3Model(
+            vllm_config=vllm_config, prefix=maybe_prefix(prefix, "model")
+        )
+
+        if get_pp_group().is_last_rank:
+            self.lm_head = ParallelLMHead(
+                config.vocab_size,
+                config.hidden_size,
+                quant_config=quant_config,
+                prefix=maybe_prefix(prefix, "lm_head"),
+            )
+            if config.tie_word_embeddings:
+                self.lm_head = self.lm_head.tie_weights(self.model.embed_tokens)
+        else:
+            self.lm_head = PPMissingLayer()
+
+        self.logits_processor = LogitsProcessor(config.vocab_size)
+        self.make_empty_intermediate_tensors = (
+            self.model.make_empty_intermediate_tensors
+        )
+
+    def embed_input_ids(self, input_ids: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return self.model.embed_input_ids(input_ids)
+
+    def forward(
+        self,
+        input_ids: torch.Tensor | None,
+        positions: torch.Tensor,
+        intermediate_tensors: IntermediateTensors | None = None,
+        inputs_embeds: torch.Tensor | None = None,
+        **kwargs,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor | IntermediateTensors:
+        return self.model(input_ids, positions, intermediate_tensors, inputs_embeds)
+
+    def compute_logits(self, hidden_states: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
+        return self.logits_processor(self.lm_head, hidden_states)
+
+    def load_weights(self, weights: Iterable[tuple[str, torch.Tensor]]) -> set[str]:
+        loader = AutoWeightsLoader(
+            self,
+            ignore_unexpected_prefixes=(
+                ["lm_head."] if self.config.tie_word_embeddings else None
+            ),
+        )
+        return loader.load_weights(weights)

Until then this PR loads the config via `trust_remote_code` from the checkpoint, and execution uses the native vLLM model, so it works with current transformers (validation in the description was run that way). Happy to follow whatever maintainers prefer: wait for #50036, or vendor `Lfm3Config` under `vllm/transformers_utils/configs/` in the meantime.

The description lists quantization and LoRA as not validated yet. I had an LFM3 port of my own that is nearly identical to this PR, so I ran those checks on it, plus IFEval, on a different GPU. The results are below in case they help review.

**Scope.** These numbers come from my own branch, not from this PR's head. The model code differs from `lfm3.py` here in only a few places:
- I don't set `ignore_unexpected_prefixes` for a tied `lm_head`.
- I don't pass `num_spec` to `short_conv_state_shape`, the same as `lfm2.py`.
- I map to `proportional` RoPE only when `partial_rotary_factor < 1`, and raise for a partial factor with a non-default `rope_type`.

None of these touches the quantized or LoRA code paths. The kernel is #64647's change plus a width guard (suggested there).

**Environment:** RTX 4070 Ti SUPER (sm_89, 16 GB), torch 2.14.0+cu130, transformers 5.22.1, Triton 3.8.0, base `3d23773f10`. Server: `vllm serve ... --trust-remote-code --max-model-len 32768 --reasoning-parser deepseek_r1`.

**Tests on this GPU:** `test_causal_conv1d.py` 324 passed, the registry/init tests 3 passed, and `test_hybrid.py -k LFM3` passed.

### GSM8K 5-shot and the generation config

| `--generation-config` | `tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, 5-shot, greedy, 256 tokens, 1319 questions |
|---|---|
| default (`auto`) | 46.2% |
| `vllm` | 41.7% |

The default 46.2% agrees with the 45.87% in the description. The checkpoint's `generation_config.json` sets `repetition_penalty: 1.1`, and with the default `--generation-config auto` the server merges it into every request, which makes up the difference. I ran the other evals with `--generation-config vllm`, so the card's sampling settings below are the only ones applied.

I also sent the first 200 questions through Transformers greedy, with the repetition penalty removed. Transformers and vLLM both scored 39.0%, and 166 of the 200 extracted answers were the same.

### Accuracy, BF16 and Liquid's quantized checkpoints

The card's settings are thinking on. GSM8K uses temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95 and top_k 20. IFEval uses lm-eval 0.4.13 `local-chat-completions` at temperature 0.6, top_p 0.95 and `max_gen_toks` 16384.

| Checkpoint | Kernel on sm_89 | GSM8K, 0-shot chat, 1319 questions | IFEval prompt strict / prompt loose / inst strict / inst loose |
|---|---|---|---|
| LFM3-1.7B (BF16) | — | 87.2 | 95.38 / 96.67 / 96.16 / 97.24 |
| LFM3-1.7B-FP8 (compressed-tensors, 128×128 blocks) | `MarlinFP8ScaledMMLinearKernel` | 86.1 | 93.90 / 96.30 / 95.08 / 96.76 |
| LFM3-1.7B-NVFP4 (ModelOpt) | `MarlinNvFp4LinearKernel` | 86.3 | 94.45 / 94.82 / 95.08 / 95.44 |

The model card gives 96.66 for IFEval.

**Loading.** Both quantized checkpoints load with no LFM3-specific code:
- Their ignore and exclude lists name the conv layers `conv.*`. Those names still match `short_conv` after the weight mapper is applied.
- The conv projections, `gate_proj` and `lm_head` stay BF16, as the model cards state.
- NVFP4 also leaves attention unquantized.

sm_89 runs both checkpoints through the weight-only Marlin kernels, so the native W8A8 block-FP8 and W4A4 NVFP4 paths on Hopper and Blackwell are not covered here.

### LoRA

The adapters are rank 8 and use the checkpoint's own module names:
- **Attention:** `q/k/v/o_proj` and `gate_proj`.
- **Conv:** `conv.in_proj` and `conv.out_proj`.
- **MLP:** `w1/w2/w3`.

Each run used 32 greedy tokens.

| Check | BF16 | FP8 | NVFP4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Zero-B adapter gives output identical to the base model | yes | yes | yes |
| Random adapter changes the output | yes | yes | yes |
| Adapter nonzero only on `conv.in_proj`/`conv.out_proj` changes the output | yes | yes | yes |
| Adapter nonzero only on `gate_proj` changes the output | yes | yes | no token flipped (see below) |

The conv-only and gate-only adapters target the two places where an adapter could be silently dropped: the `.conv.` → `.short_conv.` rename and the single-slice `in_proj` packing.

**NVFP4 gate-only.** The gate-only adapter flipped no token on NVFP4, but it is applied. Its `gate_proj` is a `ColumnParallelLinearWithLoRA`, and it shifts the logprobs by about as much as on BF16 (mean 0.02, max 0.11).

**Mixed batches.** I mixed base, zero-adapter and random-adapter requests in one batch. Compared with separate runs, the only differences were divergences at near-ties, where each token was in the other's top 5. That is expected without batch invariance.

Once this PR merges, I can follow up with a CI test for the quantized checkpoints and LoRA, if that would be useful.

**Scope.** These numbers come from my own branch ([hungho77/vllm@feat/lfm3](https://github.com/hungho77/vllm/tree/feat/lfm3)), not from this PR's head.

AI assistance (Claude) was used to write this comment and the evaluation scripts. I ran the measurements myself.
